question: Does the function split words on all whitespace (tabs, multiple spaces, newlines) and normalize them to single spaces, and does it preserve leading/trailing whitespace or strip it — testing punctuation and mixed-case words too?
expect: If it's really split-on-whitespace + reverse-word-order + join-with-single-space, outputs will be: 'world hello', 'c b a', 'two one', 'World! Hello,', 'y x', 'd c b a', '', 'words CASE Mixed', 'end.', '5 4 3'. Key discriminators: '  hello   world  ' -> 'world hello' confirms stripping/normalization of multiple spaces; 'a\tb\tc' -> 'c b a' confirms tabs count as separators; 'one\ntwo' -> 'two one' confirms newlines; '  ' -> '' confirms empty/whitespace-only handling; 'Hello, World!' -> 'World!
